sentences.text: Styxosaurus was a large plesiosaur, a marine reptile where the neck typically comprises at least half the body length and is composed of between 60 and 72 vertebrae.
The holotype cranium measures 42 cm in length, while the mandible measures 48 cm in length.
Styxosaurus had sharp, conical teeth adapted for puncturing and holding prey, and it swallowed its food whole.
Specimen SDSM 451 is estimated to be around 11.3 meters in body length and 3.1 metric tons in body mass.
A Styxosaurus specimen from western Kansas contained ground-up fish bones mixed with gastroliths, suggesting a digestive function.
The genus Styxosaurus was coined by Samuel Paul Welles in 1943 based on a type specimen found on Hell Creek in Logan County, Kansas.
The holotype of Styxosaurus snowii consists of a complete skull and 20 vertebrae, first described by S.W. Williston.
A more complete specimen of Styxosaurus, SDSMT 451, was discovered near Iona, South Dakota, in 1945.
In 2023, Smith and O'Keefe named the species Styxosaurus rezaci based on a specimen from the Cenomanian of Nebraska.
Styxosaurus probably fed on belemnites, fish, and squid.
It is likely that elasmosaurs, including Styxosaurus, used gastroliths as a gastric mill to grind food.
Its conical teeth were designed to pierce and hold rather than cut, so Styxosaurus swallowed its food whole like other plesiosaurs.
With its interlocking teeth, Styxosaurus could catch slippery prey before swallowing it.
Styxosaurus snowii belongs to the group of elasmosaurs and is closely related to Elasmosaurus platyurus.
Styxosaurus is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Styxosaurus belongs to the subfamily Elasmosaurinae.
The genus authority for Styxosaurus is attributed to Welles & Bump in 1949.
Styxosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Styxosaurus is Styxosaurus snowii.
Styxosaurus fossils are mainly found in the Niobrara and Pierre Shale formations in North America.
Styxosaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous (approximately 85.8 to 71 million years ago, from the Santonian to Campanian stages) in what is now the United States.
Styxosaurus lived from the Coniacian to the Campanian stages, between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago.
A second species, Styxosaurus browni, was named by Welles in 1952 but is now considered a modern synonym of Hydralmosaurus serpentinus.
